access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-14 (T-3553) from the museum's open-access image and object record: a pale green striped cotton and silk summer dress: black velvet ribbon bows down the bodice and in lines down the skirt, a ruffled cape collar, the skirt ending in gathered flounces. A real garment, American, not of Chicago and not of anyone drawn in the town.
note: One of the T-3553 finery references (docs/RESEARCH/finery-3553/README.md): the striped summer dress.
what_it_supplies: a striped summer cloth trimmed with black velvet ribbon and bows, and a flounced hem
what_it_does_not_supply: how any Prairie Avenue woman dressed, or the colour of any dress she owned
how often such a dress was worn on a Chicago street in 1904
